of VidhyaBharti Trust submitted a change report No.246 of 2010 and other
different Nos., which remained pending since long before it. However,

3. Present petition has been filed by the petitioners complaining
that on the one hand the delay condonation application as well
as the interim application pending before the DRT in S.A.
No.131 of 2025 are not being taken up for consideration and on
the other hand, the respondents are threatening to take
possession in pursuance to an order passed under Section 14.

interim application positively either on the next date of listing
or within a period of three weeks thereafter.
6. Till the decision on the interim application and the delay
condonation application, the respondents shall not dispossess
the petitioners from the property in question.

JUDGMENT
This Regular Second Appeal has been directed against the
judgment and decree in A.S.No.98/2012 on the file of Additional
District Court-II, Manjeri which arose out of judgment and
decree in O.S.No.275/2009 on the file of Subordinate Judge's
Court, Manjeri.
2. Appellant is the third defendant in O.S.No.275/2009.
(The parties would hereinafter be referred as per their status
before the trial court).
3. The suit was one for partition filed by the plaintiff, the
daughter of the first defendant and sister of the second
defendant. Plaint schedule property originally belonged to Pious
Sebastian, the father of the plaintiff and the brother of the third
defendant, who obtained the same as per Assignment Deed
No.534/1988 of Melatur Sub Registry Office. Pious Sebastian
died intestate on 11.03.2004 leaving behind the plaintiff and
defendants 1 and 2 as his legal heirs. Plaintiff has been residing
separately from defendants 1 and 2 and she demanded partition
of the scheduled property. There is a residential building in the
plaint schedule property, which may fetch not less than
R.S.A.No.111/2017
3
Rs.3,000/- per month as rent. The building was rented out to the
third defendant by defendants 1 & 2 without the knowledge of
plaintiff and plaintiff claimed Rs.1,000/- per month towards share
in the rent. Hence the suit has been filed claiming 1/3rd share out
of plaint schedule property together with mesne profits.
4. First defendant filed written statement contending that
she transferred her right in the plaint schedule property to the
third defendant and plaintiff had not objected the transfer.
Hence the suit is not maintainable and it is also contended that if
at all it is found that the plaint schedule property is partiable she
claims to allot her share in her favour.
5. No written statement has been filed by the 2nd
defendant.
6. Third defendant filed separate written statement
denying all the allegations in the plaint. The suit has been filed in
collusion between the plaintiff and other defendants to defeat
the interest of this defendant and cause loss and hardship to
him. The plaint schedule property has been assigned to him as
per document No.1531/1/2005 of Melatur S.R.O and he is in
absolute possession and enjoyment of the property. Neither the
R.S.A.No.111/2017
4
plaintiff nor the defendants have any right over the plaint
schedule property. Plaintiff has no cause of action and hence he
prayed for dismissal of the suit.
7. There is no oral evidence from either side. Ext.A1
marked from the side of the plaintiff. Ext.B1 marked from the
side of the third defendant.
8. Trial court on evaluation of pleadings and documents
found that first defendant as guardian of plaintiff an
tail:
f the document in the plaint the
third defendant is not expected to adduce further evidence to
prove that the transfer was for the benefit of the minor plaintiff.
37. It is to be noted that this is a case filed by the plaintiff
seeking for partition of the plaint schedule property alone. It has
already been found that in order to claim partition plaintiff ought
to have sought for cancellation of the document. None of the
decisions relied on by the learned counsel would go to the
R.S.A.No.111/2017
27
extent of holding that in a suit filed for partition the court can
mould the relief to the extent of cancelling a document without a
prayer for cancellation of the document especially when the
defendant claims right and title based on that document. The
relief for partition and setting aside a document cannot be taken
as an alternative relief or additional relief which goes in
consonance with the plaint relief already claimed as has been
held in the decisions relied on by the learned counsel. So the
contention of the learned counsel that the court can mould the
relief and grant a decree for cancelling Ext.B1 document in view
of the averments in the rejoinder filed by the plaintiff is not
sustainable and is hereby negatived.
In the result, the judgment and decree passed by the courts
below are hereby set aside and appeal allowed dismissing the
suit. Considering the facts and circumstances and relationship
between the parties, there is no order as to costs.
Sd/-

CORAM: HONOURABLE SHRI JUSTICE DHARNIDHAR JHA

HONOURABLE SHRI JUSTICE AMARESH KUMAR LAL
ORAL JUDGMENT
(Per: HONOURABLE SHRI JUSTICE DHARNIDHAR JHA)
Date: 07-08-2014
1. These appeals arise out of judgment dated 26.3.1992 by
which the two appellants, one in each of the two appeals, were held
guilty of committing offences under Sections 302/34 and 201 of the
Indian Penal Code. The appellants were heard on sentence on the
same day and they were directed to suffer rigorous imprisonment for
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.40 of 1992 dt.07-08-2014
2/9
life after having been found guilty of committing offence under
Sections 302/34 of the Indian Penal Code as also to suffer rigorous
imprisonment for seven years on account of having committed the
offence under Section 201 of the Penal Code. Appellant Raj Kumar
Sonar had separately been charged under Section 406 of the Indian
Penal Code for committing the theft of generator set and he was held
guilty also of committing that offence and was sentenced to suffer
rigorous imprisonment for three years on that count. Convicts Raj
Kumar Sonar and Bhola Baitha @ Md. Islam preferred their separate
appeals to challenge the propriety of the judgment.
2. The facts which appear from the FIR as also from the
evidence was that the informant Pashupati Nath (P.W. 12) was
running a shop of video and cassettes and used to let the video
player, television set as also a generator with some cassettes on hire
to desirous persons. It was stated that on 28.7.1988 at about 9 p.m.
appellant Raj Kumar Sonar had hired the television, the VCP and a
cassette of the film ‘Hamara Khandan’ with a generator of Bullet
make on a rental of Rs.130/- and the instruments were to be run by
the deceased Om Prakash Choudhary. On 29.7.1988, early in the
morning, the father of Om Prakash Choudhary, namely, Sukhdeo
Choudhary (P.W. 7) came to complain to the informant (P.W. 12)
that his son who had left his house in a lungi after taking his dinner
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.40 of 1992 dt.07-08-2014
3/9
to run the video show had not returned. The informant thereafter
made enquiries from appellant Raj Kumar Sonar and he stated that
the show had been run at the grease-factory situated at Mohalla
Shrighat Karimchak in Chapra and the show had been witnessed by
appellant Raj Kumar Sonar, appellant Bhola Baitha @ Md. Islam and
the third accused who was acquitted, namely, Ved Prakash Rai. The
informant went to the grease-factory with appellant Raj Kumar Sonar
and found appellant Bhola Baitha @ Md. Islam there who stated that
while the show was still going on, the deceased Om Prakash
Choudhary left the site of the show at about 3 a.m. for his house. The
informant stated that because the deceased had not come back so he
grew more suspicious and questioned appellant B
tail:
hich could be said to be of
any use so as to using as a supporting corroborating evidence to the
evidence of extra judicial confession.
7. We have very well pointed out from the very impugned
judgment that the learned trial Judge recorded that the recovery of
the sickle was of no consequence but still the seizure thereof was of
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.40 of 1992 dt.07-08-2014
9/9
immense importance along with the seizure of the generator set. We
do not wish to add anything further to what we have already noted a
bit earlier in the present judgment that there was no evidence to
indicate as to who had concealed either the generator set or the
sickle. Above all, the sickle undisputedly was not bearing a blood-
like-stain over it.
8. In our opinion, the evidence was too weak and flimsy to
raise an inference of culpability as regards the murder of Om Prakash
Choudhary. The evidence did not justify rendering the verdict of
guilt against the two appellants and passing the sentence upon them.
9. In the result, the judgment of conviction and order of
sentence dated 26.3.1992 passed by the learned 3rd Additional
Sessions Judge, Saran, Chapra in Sessions Trial No. 66 of 1989 is set
aside and the two appeals are allowed. The two appellants are
acquitted of the charges they had been found guilty of. The two
appellants are on bail. They shall stand discharged from the
liabilities of their respective bonds.
Kanchan/Sanjay

ORDER:
The writ petition is filed by the petitioners seeking for a writ of
mandamus to declare the inaction on the part of 1st respondent in not
taking any action with regard to the various irregularities committed in
the process of conducting the examinations in respect of recruitment to
the post of Lecturers in Economics in Government Degree Colleges in
A.P Collegiate Education Service, pursuant to the Notification
No:12/2009, dated 13.10.2009 Supplemental Notification No:16/2010,
dated 7.10.2010 despite bringing it to the notice of the 1st respondent
about the irregularities and mass copying and though the said issue was
widely published in the newspapers, as being illegal and arbitrary and
consequently, to direct the 1st respondent to issue fresh notification in so
far as the posts of Lecturers in Economics is concerned and to conduct
the examination in accordance with the procedure and law.
The case of the petitioners is that they are possessing requisite
qualification for recruitment to the post of Lecturers and in pursuance of
the notification No:12/2009, dated 13.10.2009 issued by the 1st
respondent, they have submitted their individual applications and
subsequently, due to the postponement of the examinations, a
supplemental notification was issued on 7.10.2010 vide notification
No:16/2010. On 14.8.2011, the examination was held and they have
also appeared for the examination. At that time, the question papers
supplied to the candidates is identical and common and therefore, the
procedure has not been following by grouping the question papers as A,
B, C and D only for the purpose of avoiding mass copying. The 4th
respondent who is the Committee Member in collusion with the
authorities of the 1st respondent for extraneous considerations, had
allotted a single center to all of the students who pursued their studies
under him (4th respondent) and thereby, the mass copying took place
and ultimately, all the students of the 4th respondent became successful
in the examinations. The aspect of mass copying was also published in
all the reputed newspapers, but no action has been taken by the 1st
respondent. Hence, the present writ petition is filed.
The question as to whether such irregularities as alleged by the
petitioners, had occurred or not, is only a mere allegation, which is no
doubt within the domain of the authorities to examine the truth or
otherwise of the same and as such, the same cannot be entertained in a
proceedings of this nature invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under
Article 226 of the Constitution of India. Therefore, the writ petition,
which is misconceived, is not maintainable and the same is liable to be
dismissed.
Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed. No costs.
__________________
Justice G.Chandraiah.

THE HON’BLE SMT. JUSTICE LALITHA KANNEGANTI
TRANSFER CRIMINAL PETITION NOs.8 and 9 of 2020
COMMON ORDER:-
Since the parties are one and the same in both the petitions,
these petitions are disposed of by this common order.
These transfer petitions are filed seeking withdrawal of
C.C.Nos.657 of 2018 and 485 of 2018 respectively from the file of
the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Puttaparthi, Ananthapuram
and transfer the same to the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate
of First Class, Kadapa.
2. The case of the petitioner, in brief is that respondent No.2
lodged a report before Bukkarayapatnam Police Station alleging
that the petitioner and another accused hit respondent No.2 with
iron rod which resulted in causing bleeding injuries and the same
was registered as crime No.37 of 2011 for the offences punishable
under Sections 324 and 506 read with 34 of I.P.C., which was
numbered as C.C.15 of 2012 which was subsequently transferred
to the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Puttaparthy and renumbered as C.C.485 of 2018. The further case
of the petitioner is that another complaint was lodged by
respondent No.2 by using the cheque which was forcibly obtained
from the petitioner and the same was registered as C.C.238 of
2012 for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instruments Act which was subsequently transferred to
learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class Magistrate, Puttaparthi
on point of jurisdiction and it was renumbered as C.C.657 of
2
2018. The petitioner who is accused in both the cases has filed
these petitions on the ground of threat faced by him in hands of
respondent No.2/complainant.
3. Heard V.R.Machavaram, learned counsel for the petitioner
and the notice sent to respondent No.2 returned with an
endorsement ‘consignment refused’ and notice sent to respondent
No.3 returned unserved.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that respondent
No.2 who is unlawful element having criminal and political
background had threatened him on 20.02.2011 while the
petitioner was sleeping in his house, as such the petitioner has
filed a complaint before Proddatur Police as well as
Superintendent of Police, Kadapa against respondent No.2 on
21.05.2015, but no action was taken. He submits that respondent
No.2 is having political clout at Puttaparthi, as such the petitioner
is apprehending that respondent No.2 and his men may do away
with his life.
5. The transfer of cases is sought only on the sole ground of life
threat in the hands of respondent No.2 and his henchmen. But his
apprehension is not supported by any material except filing copies
of reports lodged by him. Admittedly the incident took place in the
year 2015 and reports were also lodged in the same year, but
when the Police have not taken any action with regard to his
reports even after lapse of four years, the petitioner has not taken
any further steps in that regard.
3
6. The transfer petitions filed with these type of baseless
allegations cannot be entertained and hence, the same are liable to
be dismissed.
7. Accordingly the transfer criminal petitions are dismissed.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall
stand closed.
___________________________

declaring lowest bidder does not confer vested right upon the bidder,

herein has quoted abnormally low price. Even assuming that a notice
calling for explanation is directed, the petitioner cannot make out his
case, as the petitioner has quoted a very low bid, which is unrealistic.

Mr. A. Chakraborty
... For the Appellants.
Mr. S.C. Prasad
Mr. Avijit Tewary
... For the PF Authorities.
Mr. Barnamoy Basak
... For the Respondent.
1. The appellants are aggrieved by an order dated 25th
February, 2025 passed by a Single Bench of this Court.
By the said order the Single Bench having regard to the
submissions made by the learned counsel for the
appellants that they do not wish to challenge the order
under Section 14B and 7Q of the EPF Act and only wish to
pay the same by easy installments because they are not
financially sound, permitted the appellants to pray for
such installments from the respondents.
2. The Single Bench was also of the view that the
provision for appeal under Section 7(I) of the EPF Act is
beyond limitation and a writ petition cannot be entertained
beyond such period. The Single Bench was possible guided
by a decision of the Supreme Court in the case of
Assistant Commissioner (CT) LTU, Kakinada & Ors.
Vs. Glaxo Smith Kline Consumer Health Care Limited
reported in (2020) 19 SCC 681.
2
3. Learned senior counsel for the appellants Mr.
Ghoshal would submit that their counsel did not have
instructions to make such submission before the Single
Bench on the said date.
4. The proper remedy of the appellants would have
been to file an application before the Single Bench seeking
withdrawal of the offer to pay the demand of the
respondents in installments on appropriate grounds and
furnishing appropriate reasons and documents therefor.
5. In the light of the above, since the statutory period
of limitation for appeal under Section 7(I) of the EPF Act
has expired and having regard to the dicta of the Supreme
Court in the case of Assistant Commissioner (CT) LTU,
Kakinada & Ors. Vs. Glaxo Smith Kline Consumer
Health Care Limited (supra), this Court is of the view
that the order of the Single Bench calls for no interference.
6. Hence, FMA 388 of 2026 fails and hereby dismissed.
Consequently, all connected pending applications are also
dismissed.
7. Interim order, if any, shall stand vacated.
8. There shall be no order as to costs.
9. All parties shall act on the server copy of this order
duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.
(Rajasekhar Mantha, J.)
(Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J.)

Order
This writ petition has been filed against the impugned order dated
07.02.2026, wherein the 1st respondent has confirmed the order of the 2nd
respondent, who vide order dated 26.09.2025, directed the 3rd respondent and
his wife to deposit Rs.500/- as maintenance to the petitioner, and quash the
same and further direct the 1st respondent to give protection to the petitioner
from the 3rd respondent.
2. The case of the petitioner is that her husband passed away on
10.03.1992, leaving behind the petitioner and their three children namely one
son and three daughters. The petitioner being a single mother brought up the
children by working as coolie in the agricultural lands. Out of her savings, she
purchased a vacant land at Achirapakkam Village, Maduranthagam Taluk,
Chengalpattu District, measuring an extent of 19 cents. Thereafter, she
constructed a residential house and has been residing therein. On 05.04.2010,
she had sold 9 cents of land to one Kasthuri and on the very same day, also
executed a Settlement Deed settling the residential portion measuring an extent
of 10 cents in favour of her son viz., the 3rd respondent. alleging, the 3rd
respondent failed to maintain and take care of her, on 06.03.2024, she had givenhttps://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
WP No. 18508 of 2026
__________
Page3 of 6
petition under Senior Citizen Act, seeking cancellation of the settlement Deed.
After conducting enquiry, on 26.09.2025, the 2nd respondent has passed an
order, directing the 3rd respondent and his wife to deposit a sum of Rs.500/-
every month into the petitioner’s account and also directed them not to interfere
with the petitioner’s receipt of rental income of Rs.5,000/- per month. Against
the said order, the petitioner has preferred appeal before the 1st respondent.
However, the 1st respondent also confirmed the order of the 2nd respondent.

1. Heard Sri Atharva Arya and Sri Archit Rajput, learned counsel
appearing under the authority of Sri Yash Bhardwaj for the
petitioner. Sri Shishir Jain, learned counsel has put in appearance
on behalf of the respondent.
2. By means of the present petition preferred under Section 11(6)
of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the petitioner seeks
appointment of a Sole Arbitrator.
3. It is stated that the petitioner and the respondent had entered
into an agreement dated 15.10.2015 in terms whereof certain
constructions have to be raised. Clause 56 of the said agreement
contained an arbitration clause.
4. It is the case of the petitioner that though the work was done,
however, certain disputes arose in respect of payment of
outstanding bills. From time to time, the respondent had made part
payments and at the later point of time, the remaining payments
were stopped which prompted the petitioner to raise the disputes.
5. The petitioner while invoking the arbitration clause sought the
good offices of the respondent to resolve the disputes amicably,
however, no response was forthcoming from the side of the

respondents. In furtherance thereof the petitioner issued a notice
under Section 21 of the Act of 1996 dated 04.10.2023 which again
was not responded. It is in the aforesaid backdrop that the
petitioner has approached this Court for seeking appointment of an
Arbitrator.
6. Sri Shishir Jain, learned counsel for the respondent while
refuting the aforesaid submissions submitted that in so far as the
arbitration clause and its invocation is concerned, there is no
dispute between the parties. However, what has been submitted is
the fact that the petitioner had raised the dispute regarding the bills
which were paid finally to the petitioner in October, 2019 and he
had also made an endorsement indicating that all his bills stood
cleared.
7. It is further urged that in light of the aforesaid endorsement, the
petitioner cannot be permitted to raise any fresh claims. This fact
apart, even the claims sought to be raised are barred by limitation,
inasmuch as, the last payment admittedly was made in October,
2019 and period of three year expired in October, 2022. However,
in terms of Clause 56 of the Agreement, the petitioner invoked the
amicable settlement clause on 26.12.2022 and once there was no
response, the notice under Section 21 was issued on 04.10.2023
i.e much beyond the period of limitation.
8. It is thus urged that the instant petition preferred by the petitioner
is barred by limitation and no live disputes remained between the
parties, consequently, no reference can be made for arbitration.
9. The learned counsel for the petitioner responding to the
aforesaid submissions has pointed out that admittedly last payment
was made in October, 2019, however, the disputes relates to the
GST payments and claims based on escalation price.
10. It is urged that in light of the decision of the Apex Court in Re:-
Cognizance for Extension of Limitation in Suo Motu Writ
Petition No. 3 of 2020, the petitioner is entitled to seek exclusion
ARBT No. 7 of 2024
2
of two year w.e.f. 15.03.2020 till 28.02.2022 and in case if the said
period is excluded then in any case, the claim of the petitioner
would be within time.
11. It is also urged that even otherwise the issue of limitation is a
mixed question of law and fact and is not to be considered at the
stage of reference in terms of Section 11(6) of the Act of 1996
rather it can be left open to be adjudicated by the Arbitrator in
terms of Section 16 of the Act of 1996. Hence, the petition
tail:
on 21
of the Act of 1996 and admittedly there was no response from the
side of the respondents on both the aforesaid counts.
14. Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim any amount from the
respondents under the GST or escalation price or whether the
claims of the petitioner stood extinguished with the lapse of time is
an issue which will require evidence.
15. This Court in exercise of powers under Section 11(6) of the Act
of 1996 is not entitled or require to enter into these factual and
controversial aspects. It is not a case where there is a clear bar of
limitation to make the claims absolutely dead. In light of the
decisions of the Apex Court in SBI General Insurance Company
Ltd. v. Krish Spinning; (2024) 12 SCC 1, this Court finds that this
is a fit case to be referred for arbitration leaving all contentious
issues to be raised before the Arbitrator.
16. This Court proposes the name of Shri Attau Rahman
Masoodi, (Former Judge) R/o R-1, Nehru Enclave, Vishwas
Khand-3, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow, Mobile No. 9918888857 &
ARBT No. 7 of 2024
3
9415030947, to act as a Sole Arbitrator.
17. Learned counsel for the petitioner shall provide a complete set
of the paper-book to the office of this Court within a period of one
week which shall be forwarded to the proposed arbitrator to seek
his consent under Section 12(1) of the Arbitration and Conciliation
Act, 1996.
18. List this matter on 07th May, 2026 for further orders.

R.P.No.502 of 2022 was filed on the ground that
the appointed Receiver had conducted a Navaham without
seeking permission of this court and issued a letter
for the preparation of voters list as an initial step
for the purpose of conducting election. But, no such
authority was given to the Receiver appointed. He was
not authorized to do any special pooja or anything
more than that of the conduct of daily poojas of the
temple. The authority given to the Receiver is only
for the purpose of conducting daily pooja and to do
all other things in connection with the conduct of
daily pooja. The notice issued by the Receiver for
the preparation of membership list is hence without
any authority and will not have any legal effect.
With that observation, the review petition will stand
dismissed. The Receiver shall not initiate any steps
for the conduct of election or the preparation of
voters list, membership list or anything under the
guise of the power given under the order.
R.P. No.502/2022 is dismissed accordingly.

Aggrieved by the judgment dated 16.16.2007, passed by
the Additional Sessions Court, Adhoc Court No.1, Palakkad in
S.C.No.1294/2005, the accused has preferred this appeal.
2. The Trial Court convicted the accused for the offence
punishable under Section 8(2) of the Abkari Act. He was
sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two
years and pay a fine of Rs.1 Lakh.
3. The prosecution case is that on 25.12.2003 at 11.30
p.m, the accused was found possession of 1.800 litres of arrack
in a can of two liter capacity from his house at Kandiyur desom
in Kallamala Village.
4. After completing the investigation, final report was
submitted against the accused for the offence punishable under
Section 8(2) of the Abkari Act before the jurisdictional
Magistrate. The case was committed to the Sessions Court,
from where it was made over to the Trial Court. On the
CRL.A NO. 2224 OF 2007
3
appearance of the accused, charge was framed against him for
the offence punishable under Section 8(2) of the Abkari Act. The
accused pleaded not guilty to the charge, and therefore, he
came to be tried by the Trial Court for the aforesaid offence.
5. The prosecution examined PWs 1 to P5 and proved
Exts.P1 to P9 and MO1.
6. After the closure of evidence on behalf of the
prosecution, statement of the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
was recorded. He pleaded innocence. The trial Court heard the
matter under Section 232 Cr.P.C. and found evidence against
the accused, and hence he was called upon to enter on his
defence and adduce evidence, if any, he may have in support
thereof. After hearing the arguments addressed on both sides,
the Trial Court convicted the appellant/accused for the aforesaid
offence.
7. Heard Sri.Jacob Sebastian, the learned counsel for the
appellant/accused and Sri.G.Sudheer, the learned Public
Prosecutor for the respondent.
8. The learned counsel for the appellant challenged the
judgment of conviction and sentence on the ground that the
CRL.A NO. 2224 OF 2007
4
prosecution failed to establish that the contraband seized from
the place of occurrence eventually reached the Chemical
Examiner's Laboratory.
9. The learned counsel for the appellant relied on the
following circumstances to substantiate his contentions:-
(a) There is no evidence to show that the specimen
of the seal used was produced before the Court so
as to ascertain the genuineness of the sample.
(b) The various officials who handled the sample
during the course of its transit from the Court to the
Laboratory were not examined by the prosecution.
10. Exhibit P3 is the seizure mahazar. It does not contain
the nature of the seal stated to have been used by the detecting
officer. The detecting officer has not given evidence as to the
specific nature of the seal used by him. No material has been
placed before the Court to show that the specimen seal was
produced before the Court so as to enable the Court to ascertain
the genuineness of the sample produced.
11. In Bhaskaran K. v. State of Kerala and another (2020
KHC 5296), this Court held that the specimen of the seal shall
CRL.A NO. 2224 OF 2007
5
be provided in the seizure mah
tail:
rough
an excise guard by name Sri S. Jayakumar. Neither
Sri.S.Jayakumar nor the property clerk, the custodian of the
sample was examined by the prosecution to rule out the
possibility of the sample being changed or tampered with. The
inevitable consequence of this omission is that the prosecution
failed to establish that the contraband seized at the scene of
occurrence eventually reached the Chemical Examiner's
Laboratory. This view is fortified by the decision of the Apex
Court in State of Rajasthan v. Daulat Ram (AIR 1980 SC 1314).
13. The prosecution failed to establish that the contraband
seized from the place of occurrence was subjected to analysis in
CRL.A NO. 2224 OF 2007
6
the Chemical Examiner's Laboratory. Therefore, Exhibit P9,
Certificate of Chemical Analysis has no evidentiary value.
14. In Vijay Pandey v. State of U.P (AIR 2019 SC 3569)
the Apex Court held that mere production of a laboratory report
that the sample tested was the contraband substance cannot be
conclusive proof by itself and that the sample seized and that
tested have to be co-related. It is the duty of the prosecution to
establish that the sample seized and that tested are the same.
The upshot of the above discussion is that the conviction
and sentence entered by the Court below overlooking these vital
aspects of the matter cannot, therefore, be sustained. In the
result, the accused is acquitted of the offence alleged. He is set
at liberty.
The appeal is allowed as above.
Sd/-
K.BABU,
JUDGE

vested with the prisoner and is rather a privilege available to
the prisoner on fulfilling certain conditions. This is a
discretionary power which has to be exercised by the
authorities conferred with such powers under the provisions of

the claim of the prisoner for grant of parole. Consequently, the
application deserves to be dismissed and same is accordingly
dismissed.

(Order of the Court was made by MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR, J.)
This writ petition has been filed by the Public Information Officer of
this court, aggrieved by the twin orders passed by the Central Information
Commission/ second respondent dated 24.10.2016, directing the petitioner to
deal with various RTI Applications filed by the first respondent separately,
keeping in view the provisions of the Right to Information Act, 2005
(hereinafter referred to as ‘the Act’), while calling upon the petitioner to
show-cause as to why action should not be taken against him for contravening
the provisions of the Act. Through the impugned orders, the second
respondent disposed of ten complaints and four appeals filed by the first
respondent herein.
2. We have heard Mr.B.Vijay, learned counsel for the petitioner,
Mr.B.Bharathi, party-in-person and Mr.Sudhirkumar, learned Special Panel
Page 2 of 24https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
W.P.No.42137 of 2016
Counsel appearing for the second respondent and perused the entire material
on record.
3. Before dealing with the matter on merits, we deem it appropriate to
refer to some of the orders passed by this court as well as the State
Information Commission on an earlier occasion at the instance of the first
respondent herein. A learned Single Judge of this court, in W.P.No.16504 of
2014, by an order dated 19.12.2022, has been pleased to take note of 108
cases/ appeals filed by the first respondent seeking information from various
authorities, including this court, during the year 2012 alone, and observed as
under:-
“7.The conduct of the petitioner is demonstrated
from his own applications filed under the Act. It is
nothing but abuse of process of law and particular
statute, which was enacted for achieving transparency
with regard to administration. Thousands of questions
raised by the citizens taking undue advantage of the Act
will result in hanging the system and efficient
administration. It will disproportionately divert the
manpower of the administration from discharging the
normal duties of their office. Such attempt shall not be
encouraged even though the Act provides for no
limitations.
8.Therefore, the writ petition is dismissed. This is
a fit case for imposing heavy costs. However,
considering the petitioner's plight, this Court restrain
itself from doing so. No costs. Consequently, connected
miscellaneous petitions are closed.”

W.P.No.42137 of 2016

respondent allowed the above order dated 19.12.2022 to become final.

17.09.2014, a learn

conduct, causing every hindrance to the authorities under the Act in

1. At the very outset, it is to be mentioned that three
accused persons have been convicted in this case, out
of whom, appellant no. 1 Koncha Oraon has died
during pendency of this appeal and appeal on his
behalf has been abated vide order dated 19.08.2025.
So far convict Mannu Kachap, who has preferred
another appeal i.e. Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1179 of 2003
is concerned, his appeal has been abated vide order
dated 06.10.2025 as he has also died during
pendency of appeal.
2. Heard Mrs. Supriya Dayal, learned counsel for the
sole surviving appellant as well as Mr. Shiv Shankar
2026:JHHC:2283-DB
Page 2 of 15
Kumar, learned A.P.P. for the State.
3. The instant appeal is directed against the judgment of
conviction dated 08.07.2003 and order of sentence
dated 09.07.2003 passed by learned Additional
Judicial Commissioner, Fast Track Court, Ranchi in
Sessions Trial No. 498 of 1995, whereby and
whereunder, the present appellant along with two
others have been held guilty and convicted for the
offence under Section 302/34 & 201/34 of the I.P.C.
and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for
life each for the offence under Section 302/34 of the
I.P.C. and rigorous imprisonment for 5 years each for
the offences under Section 201/34 of the I.P.C. Both
the sentences were directed to run concurrently.
FACTUAL MATRIX
4. The factual matrix giving rise to this appeal is that on
15.05.1995 in the night informant, Sanjay Kachap
along with his sisters Geeta Kachap and Reeta
Kachap, Kuldeep Oraon and Sushil Oraon (deceased)
went to fetch Manda Mela in his village. In the said
Mela, Koncha, Raju Lakra and Mannu Kachhap were
singing and dancing. It is further alleged that Sushil
Oraon was sitting beside Geeta, sister of the
informant and on seeing this, the accused persons at
about 2:45 A.M. asked Sushil to accompany them and
took away Sushil Oraon with them. It is alleged that
2026:JHHC:2283-DB
Page 3 of 15
at about 6:00 A.M. when informant along with his
sisters Geeta and Reeta and Kuldeep were returning
to their home then they found accused persons
coming towards the Bahiyar, then they asked about
Sushil Oraon. The accused persons did not tell about
the Sushil Oraon, but said that they should go to
their own house and thereafter, they would come to
know about Sushil. It is further alleged that after
considerable lapse of time when Sushil did not return
either to the informant or to his own sister’s house,
then informant along with Kuldeep searched him and
reached in Bahiyar of the Village situated towards
north east and found shoes of deceased near the well
of Koka Oraon and when they saw into well, a dead
body was floating. The dead body of the deceased was
brought out which was of Sushil Oraon, who had
sustained injuries on cheeks, nose and head. The
police also approached the place of occurrence, where
fardbeyan of the informant Sanjay Kachhap (P.W.-3)
was recorded. It is also alleged that there was love
affairs between Geeta Kachhap and Raju Lakra and
Raju Lakra always used to say about marriage with
her and seeing Sushil Oraon with his sister Geeta on
15.05.1995, the plan of murder of Sushil was
hatched.
5. On the basis of above fardbeyan, Doranda P.S. Case

brought on record that the deceased was acquainted
with the accused persons and due to friendship or
any other reason, he went with them.
In the aforesaid circumstances, we are unable to
accept the theory of last seen as propounded by the
prosecution only on the basis of sole testimony of
P.W.-3, who himself appears to be a doubtful witness
and not reliable at all.
17. In view of the aforesaid discussions and reasons, we

committed serious error of law in relying upon the

aside the impugned judgment and order of conviction
and sentence of the appellant and acquit him from the
charges levelled against him.
18. Accordingly, the impugned judgment of conviction
and order of sentence of the appellant is hereby set
aside.
19. This appeal is allowed.
20. The appellant is on bail. He is discharged from the
liability of bail bond and sureties shall also
discharged.
21. Pending I.A., if any, stand disposed of.
22. Let a copy of this judgment along with trial court
record be sent back to the court concerned for
information and needful.

Date of hearing & delivery of
Judgment & order : 23.09.2016.
Whether Fit for Reporting : Yes/No.
JUDGMENT & ORDER(ORAL)
By filing this writ petition the petitioner prayed for the
following reliefs:-
(i) Issue Rule NISI upon the respondents to show cause as
to why a writ of Certiorari or in the nature thereof shall
not be issued cancelling/quashing the Notification dated
21.5.2011.(Annexure-P/7)
AND
(ii) As to why Clause-viii of para-4 of the Notification
dated 2.2.2010(Annexure-P/6) and Memo dated 4.1.2013
(Annexure-P/9) shall not be cancelled/quashed;
AND
(iii) As to why the Memorandum dated 4.1.2013 shall not
be cancelled being arbitrary, unreasonable, unauthorized
and discriminatory one;
(iv) Issue writ of Mandamus or in the nature thereof
commanding upon the State respondents to restore
3(three) non compounded increments with arrears
already given to the petitioner after acquiring the Ph.D
Degree and withdrawn subsequently in arbitrary and
unreasonable, unconstitutional and Whimsical manner.
(v) In the interim pass order restraining the State
respondents from recovering any amount from the
petitioner consequent upon the arbitrary, illegal and
unconstitutional withdrawal of the 3(three) non-
WP(C) No.326 of 2013 Page 2 of 5
compounded increments from the pay of the petitioner
following the Memorandum dated 4.1.2013 (Annexure-
P/10);
(vi) Any other appropriate order or direction as this
Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper may kindly be
passed.
2. Heard learned senior counsel, Mr. S.M. Chakraborty
assisted by learned counsel, Ms. P. Sen for the petitioner and learned
Addl. G.A., Mr. S. Chakraborty for the respondents.
3. At the very outset learned senior counsel, Mr.
Chakraborty submitted that the case of the petitioner is well covered
by the judgment dated 15.10.2015 passed by this Court in WP(C)
No.374 of 2011. According to Mr. Chakraborty the relief which the
petitioner sought in this writ petition has already been given to the
petitioners of WP(C) No.374 of 2011 and the said WP(C) No.374 of
2011 was disposed of with directions to submit a representation to
the respondent No.3, the Director of Higher Education seeking the
relief.
4. In WP(C) No.374 of 2011 there were four petitioners and
according to Mr. chakraborty those petitioners and the present
petitioner are similarly situated. That writ petition was disposed of
with the following directions:-
“(10) Mr. Chakraborty, learned Addl. G.A., appearing for
the State respondents submits that he has no
information whether as per the scheme, the petitioners
are not entitled to the benefit, as prayed for, or not. He
is also not in a position to say whether Dr. Anjali
WP(C) No.326 of 2013 Page 3 of 5
Chakraborty, Dr. Shyamal Debnath and others were
provided three (3) non compounded increments for
acquiring Ph.D. or not, as stated by the petit
tail:
.3 and
considering that representation those petitioners have been allowed
the relief sought by them and that the present petitioner is similarly
situated.
WP(C) No.326 of 2013 Page 4 of 5
6. Learned Addl. G.A., Mr. S. Chakraborty fairly submitted
that if the present petitioner and the petitioners of WP(C) No.374 of
2011 are similarly situated in that case the present petitioner may
make representation ventilating her grievance sighting the case of
the others for consideration of respondent No.3 and in that case the
respondent No.3 will definitely consider the prayer according to law.
7. In view of the above submission of the learned counsel of
the both side, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction that the
petitioner shall submit a representation to the Director of Higher
Education (respondent No.3) stating her grievance and also showing
the names of other similarly situated persons who have been
provided the benefit as per their claim, by the respondents and such
petition should be made within 15 days from today and the
respondent No.3 shall consider the same within one month from the
date of making representation on merit and the petitioner should
enclose a copy of the Judgment dated 15.10.2015 in WP(C) No.374 of
2011 and also mention the names of other similarly situated persons
who have been given the similar benefits supported by document, if
any.
8. With the above direction, the writ petition stands
disposed of.
JUDGE

Party Name : BIRALAL DEBBARMA Vs THE STATE OF TRIPURA
THE HONBLE MR JUSTICE U. B. SAHA
The instant application is filed by the convict appellant-petitioner for suspension of
sentence dated 10.12.2012 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, West Tripura, Agartala,
in Case No. ST 112 of 2012, wherein, the convict-appellant petitioner was convicted under
Section 304 Part-II of the IPC and sentenced to suffer RI for 8 years.
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and also perused the impugned
judgment in the connected appeal being Crl. A(j). No. 25 of 2015. According to this Court,
this is not a fit case where the order of sentence should be suspended. Accordingly, the
prayer for suspension of the order of sentence dated 10.12.2012 is rejected.

head:
SPA No. 220 of 2016
Hon’ble Rajiv Sharma, J.
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Dy.A.G. for the
State/appellants.
Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate for
the respondent.
Heard.
On due consideration, delay
condonation application (CLMA No.8336
of 2016) is allowed. Delay in filing the
appeal is condoned.
This special appeal is preferred
against the judgment dated 05.10.2015,
passed by learned Single Judge in WPSS
No.2401 of 2001.
“Key facts”, necessary for the
adjudication of this appeal are that the
respondent was appointed as a Peon on
14.10.1998. He was regularized on
08.10.1999. The services of the petitioner
were terminated along with one Atar
Singh vide order dated 08.12.1999. Atar
Singh filed a writ petition bearing WPSS
No.1202 of 2008 and the same was
allowed by learned Single Judge on
01.08.2011.
It is not in dispute that the
judgment dated 01.08.2011 has attained
the finality.
By the judgment, under challenge,
learned Single Judge in WPSS No. 2401 of
2001 has quashed the termination order
of the respondent/petitioner by relying
upon the judgment dated 01.08.2011
passed in WPSS No. 1202 of 2008.
In view of this, there is no
illegality in the impugned judgment dated
05.10.2015, passed by learned Single
Judge in WPSS No.2401 of 2001. The
appeal fails and the same is hereby
dismissed.
Pending application, if any, stands
disposed of.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) (Rajiv Sharma, J.)
23.10.2017
NISHANT

On mention case is taken out of turn.
The instant contempt petition against respondent-Islamic
University of Science & Technology, filed by the petitioner, has been pending
before this Court since the year 2022 along with the connected writ petitions.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn the attention of this
Court to a Notification G.S.R 471 (E) dated 2nd August 2024 issued by
Department of Personnel & Training (Ministry of Personnel, Public
Grievances and Pensions) Government of India, whereby in exercise of the
powers conferred by sub-section 2 of section 14 of the Administrative
Tribunals Act, 1985, ten Universities of Union Territory of J&K, including the
respondent-Islamic University of Science & Technology have been included in
the Schedule at Serial Nos. 220 to 229 conferring the jurisdiction in terms of
sub section (3) of section 14 of the Act, upon Central Administrative Tribunal
(CAT) with regard to such petitions.
In view of aforestated Notification with regard to jurisdiction of this
Court, being ousted, the present contempt petition along with connected writ
petitions on hand are ordered to be transferred to Central Administrative
Tribunal, Srinagar Bench for further proceedings along with CMs, if any.
Registry is directed to send the record of all the petitions to CAT, Srinagar,
retaining a scanned copy thereof for record.
The parties are directed to cause their appearance before the CAT,
Bench, Srinagar, on 9th October, 2024.
Disposed of.
(MA CHOWDHARY)

RAM HIRDYA MAHTO SON OF RAMSWARTH MAHTO
Versus
STATE OF BIHAR
-----------
2. 23.12.2009 Heard learned Counsel for the petitioner and the State.
The petitioner seeks bail in a case instituted for the
offence under Sections 20, 21 and 22 of the N.D.P.S. Act.
The prayer for bail was earlier rejected by an order
dated 28.6.2006 passed in Cr.Misc.No.24490 of 2006 and the
petitioner has renewed his prayer for bail after having remained in
custody since 12.9.2005.
Taking into consideration the fact that the recovery of
21 kg. ganja was not from the conscious possession of the
petitioner and up till now only six witnesses have been examined
out of ten and no witness has been examined after 2007, let the
petitioner above named be released on bail on furnishing bail bond
of Rs.5,000/- (Five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount
each to the satisfaction of 3rd Addl. Sessions Judge, East
Champaran, Motihari in Darpa P.S.case No.26 of 2005 (N.D.P.S.
case No.77 of 2005), subject to the conditions (i) that one of the
bailors will be a close relative of the petitioner who will give an
affidavit genealogy as to how he is related with the petitioner and
(ii) that the petitioner will be well represented on each date and if
he fails to do so on two consecutive dates, his bail will be liable to
be cancelled.
Narendra/ ( Anjana Prakash, J. )

ORDER:-
This petition is filed under Sections 437 and 439 of Code of the
Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short ‘Cr.P.C.’) seeking regular bail to
the petitioner/A-8 in connection with Crime No.29 of 2021 of Sileru
Police Station, Visakhapatnam District, wherein the petitioner is
alleged to have committed the offence punishable under Section 8(c)
r/w 20(b)(ii)(C) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances
Act, 1985 (for brevity “NDPS Act”).
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner/accused and learned
Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.

investigation is pending, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the
accused.

liberty is given to the accused to renew the bail application after
completion of statutory period.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall
stand closed.

No.278 of 2022, corresponding to G.R. No.626 of 2023, S.T. No.334 of 2023, for
the offences registered under Sections 366-A/34/323/341/504/34 of the Indian
Penal Code, pending in the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-III,
Sahibganj.

on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/-(Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two
sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions
Judge-III, Sahibganj, in connection with Borio P.S. Case No.278 of 2022,
corresponding to G.R. No.626 of 2023, S.T. No.334 of 2023.

U. C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. Rajendra Singh, Advocate holding brief
of Mr. G. C. Kandpal, Advocate present for the
applicant.
Mr. V. S. Pal, A.G.A. with Mr. D. K. Bankoti
and Mr. Sidhartha Bisht, Brief Holder present for
the State.
Applicant – Mohd. Faijan seeks bail in
connection with F.I.R. no.376 of 2016, under
Sections 379, 411, 413 IPC, P.S. Kashipur, District
Udham Singh Nagar.
Heard learned counsel for the parties,
considered the grounds taken in the bail application
and perused the documents on record.
An FIR was lodged on 07.10.2016 against the
unknown thieves in relation to an incident which
took place on 04.10.2016. It was alleged in the FIR
that the chasis and engine of a safari car was stolen
away by the miscreants. Applicant was arrested on
25.11.2016 and, since then, he is in jail.
Learned State counsel opposed the bail of the
applicant on the grounds, inter alia, that the
applicant will flee away from justice if he is granted
bail. In reply thereto, learned counsel for the
applicant submitted that he will furnish reliable
sureties if he is granted bail.
Considering the above facts and
circumstances, a case of bail is made out in favour
of the present applicant. The bail application is
allowed.
Let the accused-applicant be released on bail
on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two
reliable sureties each of the like amount to the
satisfaction of the Magistrate concerned.
(U. C. Dhyani, J.)
Dated 10.03.2017
Rawat

head:
Item No. 41 & 42
A.B. No. 41 of 2017
With
A.B. No. 42 of 2017
BEFORE
HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. RAMALINGAM SUDHAKAR
19.06.2018
Heard Mr. Th. Ibohal, learned senior counsel for the petitioner;
and Mr. Athouba Khaidem, learned P.P. for the respondents.
Both the petitions were filed for grant of anticipatory bail. In both
the cases, interim anticipatory bail order was granted on 06.12.2017 in the
following manner:
“In the meantime, in the event of arrest of the petitioner in
connection with FIR No. 28 (10) 2017 KJM P.S. u/s 326/354/427/506/34
IPC, he may be released on bail by executing a personal bond of Rs
20,000/- (twenty thousand) only in cash with surety of like amount to
the satisfaction of the arresting authority.”
Mr. Th. Ibohal, learned senior counsel states that the accused
persons appeared before the Investigating Officer, and have been co-
operating with the enquiry.
Today, when the matter is listed, Mr. Athouba Khaidem, learned
P.P. states that the Investigating Officer may be permitted to summon the
accused persons as when required till appropriate charge sheet is filed if the
case is made out.
In view of the same, both the petitions stand allowed by making
absolute the interim anticipatory bail order granted on 06.12.2017.
The accused persons shall report before the Investigating Officer
as and when required.
Both the petitions stands disposed of accordingly.
CHIEF JUSTICE
Sandeep

Mr. Tarun Lakhera, Advocate for the
applicant.
Mr. R.K. Sah, Dy.A.G. along with

Chaudhary, Brief Holder for the State.
Applicant-Gulam Mohmmad@Azad,
who is in jail in connection with case crime
no. 199 of 2016 under Sections 8/20 of
N.D.P.S. Act, registered at Police Station-
Sahaspur, District Dehradun, has sought his
release on bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties,
considered the grounds taken up in the bail
application and perused the documents
brought on record.
390 gms of Charas was allegedly
recovered from the possession of the
applicant, which is far less than the
commercial quantity. Applicant is in jail since
13.8.2016 and has no previous criminal
history.
Learned counsel for the applicant
submitted that many mandatory provisions of
the NDPS Act have been observed by breach.
Considering the facts and circumstances
as also the grounds taken up in the bail
application, the Court is of the opinion that
the applicant should now be enlarged on bail.
Bail application is allowed. Let the
applicant be enlarged on bail on his executing
a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction
of the Special Judge concerned.
If at any point of time, it is found that the
applicant is misusing the bail, the learned
Special Judge shall be at liberty to cancel his
bail in accordance with law.
(U.C. Dhyani, J.)
07.10.2016
Pooja

head:
MCRC-6232-2016
(RAJESH Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH)
12-04-2016
Shri Ramesh Tamrakar, counsel for the applicant.
Ms. Manjeet Chuckal, PL for the respondent /State.
This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of
Cr.P.C. for grant of bail. First application (M.Cr.C. No. 14661/2015)
was dismissed for want of prosecution on 28.8.2015 and second
application (M.Cr.C. No. 15269/2015) was dismissed as not pressed on
8.9.2015 with liberty to renew the prayer after six months.
The applicant is in custody since 12.8.2015 in connection with Crime
No. 348/2015 registered at P.S. Babai, District Hoshangabad for
offences punishable under Sections 307, 452, 294, 323, 506/34 of the
IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that co-accused Mangilal
has been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 22.3.2016
passed in M.Cr.C. No. 4282/2016 and the period of 6 months as
granted by this Court while rejecting earlier application, has also been
elapsed. The applicant is in custody for about 8 months. In view of the
above, prayer is made to enlarge the applicant on bail on the ground of
parity.
Learned counsel for the State opposes the application.
On due consideration of facts and circumstances of the case, this court
deems it proper to grant bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, the application is allowed. Applicant Rajesh is directed to
be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of
Rs.30,000/- with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction
of JMFC concerned or CJM for his appearance in the trial Court on the
dates so fixed by that Court during the trial. It is directed that the
applicant shall comply the provisions of Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
(J.K. MAHESHWARI)
JUDGE

***
THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION IS FILED UNDER
SECTION 397 (1) R/W SECTION 401 OF CR.P.C., PRAYING TO SET
ASIDE THE JUDGMENT DATED 19.03.2020 IN CRIMINAL APPEAL
NO.08/2019 BY THE X ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS
JUDGE, BELAGAVI WHEREIN CONFIRMED THE JUDGMENT DATED
14.12.2018 PASSED BY THE V-JMFC, BELAGAVI IN CC NO.2008/2017
FOR OFFENCE UNDER SECTION 138 OF N.I. ACT AND THEREBY
ACQUIT THE PETITIONERS/ACCUSED.
- 2 -
CRL.RP No.100217/2021
THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION COMING ON FOR
ADMISSION AND THE SAME HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED
FOR JUDGMENT ON 23.06.2023, THIS DAY, THE COURT
PRONOUNCED THE FOLLOWING:
ORDER
Revision petitioner/accused feeling aggrieved by the
judgment of First Appellate Court on the file of X
Additional Sessions Judge, Belagavi, in Crl.A No.8/2019,
dated 19.03.2020 confirming the judgment of Trial Court
in CC No.2008/2017 on the file of JMFC V, Belagavi, dated
14.12.2018 preferred this revision petition.
2. Heard the arguments of both sides.
3. On careful perusal of oral and documentary evidence
placed on record by complainant, it would go to show that
complainant entered into a registered agreement of sale
dated 25.09.2014 with accused for purchasing flat No.5 in
Gowri Apartments for total consideration of Rs.15,00,000/-
Out of the said consideration amount complainant paid an
amount of Rs.10,00,000/-. However, the sale deed was
not executed by accused. Complainant issued notice
- 3 -
CRL.RP No.100217/2021
dated 07.06.2017 to execute the sale deed by receiving
balance consideration. Accused gave evasive reply dated
26.07.2017. However, accused issued cheque dated
22.06.2017 for Rs.10,00,000/- Ex.P.1. Complainant
presented the said cheque for encashment through his
banker and same was dishonored vide bank endorsement
as "Account Closed" Ex.P.2. Complainant issued demand
notice dated 18.07.2017 Ex.P.3 and the same is duly
served Ex.P.7. Accused replied to the said notice Ex.P.8.
4. The Trial Court after appreciation of evidence on
record, convicted accused for the offence under Section
138 of N.I Act and the same is confirmed by First
Appellate Court.
5. Learned counsel for revision petitioner has contended
that signature of accused on the cheque Ex.P.1 is denied
and no proper opportunity was given to lead evidence of
accused. The Trial Court recorded the plea of accused and
statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. on the appearance of
accused on 19.10.2017 itself. PW.1 was examined on
- 4 -
CRL.RP No.100217/2021
12.09.2017 and he was cross-examined on 12.06.2018,
03.07.2018 and 09.07.2018. PW.2 was examined on
27.04.2018 and he was cross-examined on 01.08.2018.
PW.1 was recalled for chief-examination and cross-
examined on 25.08.2018. The material evidence in the
form of PWs.1 and 2 were not put to accused during
course of his 313 Cr.P.C statement to explain the
circumstances appearing against him. The approach of
Trial Court in recording 313 Cr.P.C. statement on the day
of appearance itself would defeat the very purpose and
object of recording statement of accused under Section
313 of Cr.P.C. The First Appellate Court also did not
appreciate the said fact and held that it is an irregularity
under Section 465 of Cr.P.C. which does not prejudice the
defence of accused in any manner and the said finding has
no recognition under law.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent seeks to
justify the judgment
tail:
sed's plea is
vitiated."
Therefore, in view of the principles enunciated in the
aforementioned judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court and this
Court, recording of statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
on the day of appearance of accused is a serious
irregularity which renders the entire proceedings from the
stage of recording accused's plea vitiated.
12. Therefore, in view of the reasons recorded above, the
procedure adopted by Trial Court recording statement of
accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. on the day of
appearance much before the conclusion of complainant
side cannot be legally sustained in view of clear mandate
of law in terms of Section 313(1)(b) of Cr.P.C. The Courts
below have recorded contrary finding regarding the
- 11 -
CRL.RP No.100217/2021
procedure adopted by Trial Court for trial of summons case
and in recording statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
Therefore, interference of this Court is required.
Consequently, proceed to pass the following;
Order
The Criminal Revision petition filed by the revision
petitioner is hereby allowed.
The impugned order of Trial Court as well as First
Appellate Court are set aside.
The matter is remitted back to Trial Court to consider
the matter afresh on merits, in accordance with law.
In order to expedite the matter, both parties are
directed to appear before Trial Court on 20.09.2023. The
Trial Court is directed to dispose of the matter within a
period of six months from the date of receipt of copy of
this order.
Sd/-

Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh-I,J.
Heard Sri Harish Chandra Mishra, learned counsel for the
applicants, and Sri Rishi Chaddha, learned A.G.A. for the State
and perused the record.
This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking bail
in Case Crime No. 58 of 2020, under Sections 323, 504 & 308
of I.P.C., Police Station Babina, District Jhansi, during the
pendency of trial.
Learned counsel for the applicants has argued that the accused
applicants have been falsely implicated. It is next argued that
general allegation has been levelled against all the four accused
named in the F.I.R. of having caused injuries to the father of the
informant. Injury memo is annexed at page no. 31 & 32 of the
paper book. With respect to the injury no. 4, the X-ray was
advised but the same has not been annexed. It is next argued
that the wife of the applicant no. 1 had moved an application to
S.H.O. of P.S. Babina against the informant and his brother that
his daughter was being teased and abused by them because of
which due to animosity, this false case has been slapped. It is
further argued that he is apprehending imminent arrest by the
police. The applicants have no criminal history. If the accused
applicants are released on anticipatory bail, they will not misuse
the liberty of bail and shall cooperate in the investigation.
Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for
granting bail but could not controvert the aforesaid fact.
Looking to the fact that no specific role has been assigned to the
accused applicant and the offence is punishable with less than
seven year of imprisonment, taking into consideration the
gravity of accusation, there being no criminal antecedents of the
applicant and there being no possibility of his fleeing from
justice, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the
case, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail
in this case.
In the event of arrest of the applicants Nemi Chandra alias
Nemi Chand and Dilip alias Kalu involved in Case Crime No.
58 of 2020, under Sections 323, 504 & 308 of I.P.C., Police
Station Babina, District Jhansi, shall be released on anticipatory
bail till the submission of police report if any under section 173
(2) Cr.P.C. before the competent Court on their furnishing a
personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like
amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the
police station concerned with the following conditions.
(i) the applicants shall make themselves available for
interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) the applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make any
inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the
facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her/them from disclosing
such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) the applicants shall not leave India without the previous
permission of the Court and if he has passport the same shall be
deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P. concerned.

shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation

Hon'ble Siddharth,J.
Heard Sri Rajendra Prasad Tiwari, learned counsel for the
applicant; Sri Hare Krishna Tripathi, learned counsel for the
informant and learned A.G.A for the State.
Counter affidavit filed by learned A.G.A is taken on record.
This is second bail application of the applicant.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected on
28.07.2020 by the coordinate Bench of this Court which is not
available now.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant
is in jail since 28.08.2019. He had no prior criminal history. Before
the trial Court, four prosecution witnesses have been examined and
nine prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The other
witnesses are not appearing since 26.04.2022 before the trial
Court. The applicant is in jail since 28.08.2019 and has no criminal
history to his credit.
On the other hand learned A.G.A has opposed the prayer for bail.
Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of
the accused; submissions of the learned counsel for the parties
noted above; finding force in the submissions made by the learned
counsel for the applicant; keeping view the uncertainty regarding
conclusion of trial; one sided investigation by police, ignoring the
case of accused side; applicant being under-trial having
fundamental right to speedy trial; larger mandate of the Article 21
of the Constitution of India; considering the dictum of Apex Court
in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil vs. C.B.I., passed in S.L.P
(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021; considering 5-6 times overcrowding in
jails over and above their capacity by the under trials and without
expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of
the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail. The bail
application is allowed.
Let the applicant, Gyanedra @ Bhajju, involved in Case Crime No.
124 of 2019, under Sections- 452, 376-D, 307, 34 IPC, Police
Station- Lahchura, District- Jhansi, be released on bail on his
furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like
amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to
following conditions. Further, before issuing the release order, the
sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the
witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he
shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence
when the witnesses are present in Court. In case of default of this
condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of
liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on
each date fixed, either personally or as directed by the Court. In
case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may
proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal
Code.
(iv) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and
in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82
Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the Court
on the date fixed in such proclamation then the Trial Court shall
initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law under

deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the
Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and
proceed against him in accordance with law.

05/20.09.2022 Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.P.P. for the
State.
This bail application has been filed on behalf of the abovenamed
applicants with prayer to release on bail in connection with Giridih Town P.S.
Case No.98 of 2022 registered under Sections 304-B/34 of the Indian Penal Code
pending in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Giridih.
Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that as per F.I.R.
allegations, the marriage of sister of the informant was solemnized with Pankaj
Kumar in June, 2021 and for demand of dowry, the sister of the informant was
tortured. On 29.05.2022, the informant received an information over his mobile
phone that his sister had committed suicide. Indeed, the dowry death of sister of
the informant was caused.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant
nos.1 and 2 are father-in-law and mother-in-law of the deceased respectively. It
is further submitted that there is no evidence in regard to demand of any dowry
and torturing the sister of the informant for non-fulfilment of the same. So far as
the cause of death is concerned, it was asphyxia due to hanging. In view of
paragraph 5 of the case-diary, the deceased had committed suicide by bolting
the door from inside and the door was broken, thereafter, her hanged dead body
was brought out. The deceased had committed suicide on account of depression
as soon before the occurrence she was operated with fibroid.
Learned A.P.P. appearing on behalf of the State vehemently
opposed the contentions made by the learned counsel for the applicant.
In view of the submissions made and materials on record, the bail
application of the applicant is hereby allowed. Let the applicant be released on
bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.30,000/-(Rupees Thirty Thousand) with two
sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned in aforesaid
case.
(Subhash Chand, J.)

3. Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that, the
applicant is not involved in commission of offence as alleged
in the FIR and therefore, looking to the role of the applicant
and nature of the allegations, the applicant is required to be
enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable terms and
Page 1 of 4

4. On the other hand, learned APP appearing for the respondent –
State opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and
gravity of the offence.
5. In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the
nature of allegations, this Court is of the opinion that,
discretion is required to be exercised to enlarge the applicant
on regular bail. This Court has considered the following facts
while exercising discretion in favour of the applicant :-
i. Investigation is over and charge-sheet is filed.
ii. The applicant is in jail since 27.10.2021.
iii. Quantity of contraband article i.e. Ganja was not
recovered from the applicant. Learned advocate for the

recovered from the co-accused was in small quantity.

Order
08/08/2025
1. The instant bail application has been filed under Section 483
of BNSS, on behalf of the petitioner, who has been arrested in
connection with FIR No.134/2025 registered at Police Station
Kotwali Sawai Madhopur, District Sawai Madhopur (Raj.) for the
offences punishable under Sections 303(2) of BNS & Section 4/21
of Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act, 1957.
After completion of investigation, police filed charge-sheet in this
matter.
2. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the
accused-petitioner has falsely been implicated in this case.
Learned counsel submits that alleged offences are triable by
Magistrate. Trial of the case will take considerable time in its
conclusion. Petitioner is in custody since his date of arrest and
[2025:RJ-JP:30610] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-9101/2025]
further custody of the petitioner would not serve any fruitful
purpose.
3. Learned Public Prosecutor opposes the submissions made by
learned counsel for the petitioner.
4. I have considered the contentions.
5. Having regard to the totality of the facts and circumstances
of the case; considering the arguments advanced by both the
parties, as also the fact that alleged offences are triable by
Magistrate; trial will take time as well as looking to the custody
period, but without commenting anything on the merits/demerits
of the case, I deem it proper to allow the bail application.
6. This bail application is accordingly allowed and it is directed
that accused-petitioner - Mansingh S/o Ramraj, shall be
released on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum
of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) together with two
sureties in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand
Only) each to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court with the
stipulation that he shall appear before that Court and any court to
which the matter is transferred, on all subsequent dates of hearing
and as and when called upon to do so.
7. It is made clear that the accused-petitioner shall not involve
in any other offence(s) during currency of the bail and he shall
mark his presence in first week of every month in the concerned
police station, till trial is concluded.
8. Concerned SHO is directed to maintain a register recording
the attendance of the petitioner, as directed above. In case the
petitioner fails to mark his presence in the concerned police
[2025:RJ-JP:30610] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-9101/2025]
station, as directed above, the concerned SHO is directed to
immediately report the matter to the concerned Court in this
regard.
9. If breach of any of these conditions is reported or come to
the notice of the Court, the same shall alone be a reason for the
trial Court to cancel the bail granted to him by this Court.
10. Office is directed to send copy of this order to the concerned
SHO for necessary compliance.
11. The observation made herein above is only for decision of
the instant bail application and would not have any impact on the
trial of the case in any manner.

1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Apprehending their arrest in connection with Hiranpur P.S.
Case No. 47 of 2023 instituted under Sections 406, 420, 409, 417/34
of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioners have moved to this Court for
grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
3. As per FIR, allegation is that petitioners along with other
co-accused persons have misappropriated government money without
doing their respective work. It is alleged that amount entered in
measurement book for the construction of Irrigation well in the land
of Birsa Roy is Rs. 2,58,353.00 and amount withdrawn is Rs.
3,23,212.00 while the actual work is worth Rs. 1,01,107.00.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that
petitioners are innocent and have committed no offence at all rather
they have been falsely implicated in this case. It is submitted that
petitioners are co-operating in the investigation in compliance of
notice under Section 41(A) Cr.p.c. It is lastly submitted that the
petitioners undertake to further co-operate with the investigation of
the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be
imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners may be extended the privilege of anticipatory
bail.
5. Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the
prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioners but fairly admitted that
work under scheme has already been completed and petitioners are
also complying and co-operating in the investigation.
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the
nature of allegation coupled with materials on record, I am inclined to
grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioners. Accordingly, the
petitioners are directed to surrender in the Court below within four
weeks from today and in the event of their arrest or surrendering, they
will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/-

connection with Hiranpur P.S. Case No. 47 of 2023 with the condition

before the investigating officer as and when noticed by him and
furnish their mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with
an undertaking that they will not change their mobile number during
the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down
under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Vadaj Police Station, Dist. Ahmedabad, for the offences
punishable under Sections 397, 302, 34, 120B of IPC and under
Section 25(1-B), 27(1) of Arms Act.
3. It is the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that he is
suffering confinement since 22.03.2018. He further submitted that
the applicant has not alleged to have played any vital role in the
alleged offence. Hence, further detention of the applicant is
unwarranted.
4. Learned APP has opposed the bail application contending that,
considering the conduct of the applicant and nature of accusation,
Page 1 of 3

5. Having carefully considered the chargesheet case papers and perusal
of the impugned order passed by the Sessions Court concerned, it
prima-facie appears that the applicant herein did not have
participated in the alleged offence as well as the murder as employee
of the Angadia Firm. The only role attributable to present applicant
is to the effect that he being rikshaw driver, he accompanied to the
co-accused to demonstrate rekee. Except this, nothing brought on
record to indicate that the applicant is involved in the alleged
offence. Till date, charge is not framed in the trial Court. The

Heard through Video Conferencing.
Shri Rakesh Singh Bhadoria, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Tarun Pagare, learned Panel lawyer for the respondent/State.
Heard, Case-diary perused.
This is an application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code,
1973, filed by the applicant for grant of bail during trial.
The applicant is facing trial in connection with Crime No.159 of 2015,
registered at Police Station-Khudel, District-Indore, concerning offence
under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 & 120 of IPC, 1860. The applicant is in jail
since 20.12.2021.
As per prosecution story, complainant purchased three trucks through
financing of Shriram Finance Company, however, he could not pay the
installments within the stipulated time hence he intimated the finance company
to take back the trucks. The manager of Shriram Finance Company,
Ragvendra Sharma informed that he will take back the trucks through agent.
Thereafter co-accused persons pretending themselves as agent took back the
trucks of complainant. Later on, on being enquired by the complainant, it
was found that the trucks did not reached the yard of Shriram Financing
Company. On the basis of which FIR has been registered for the aforesaid
offence against the accused persons. The applicant is implicated on the basis
of memo of co-accused persons recorded under Section 27 of Indian
Evidence Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is
innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present crime. Applicant is
arraigned in the matter only on the basis of memo of co-accused persons
recorded under Section 27 of Indian Evidence Act. Co-accused Pradeep and
Deepak have already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated

2. The case of the prosecution is that, on getting a secret
information regarding the possession of illicit arrack, the Police
conducted a search in the house and premises of the petitioner
herein on 22.02.2016 at 10.15 p.m. From beneath a heap of hay
near cattle shed adjoining the house, collected 300 ml arrack and
326 litres of koda kept in 10 cannas were recovered. Alleging
that the petitioner herein had kept it and she being the owner,
crime was registered. She seeks pre-arrest bail.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that
the recovery was from a place which was accessible to the
outsiders and that too on the basis of a prior information. The
counsel also contended that the search was conducted during
night and the possibility of she being implicated by planting of
articles cannot be ruled out. It was further contended that she
was not involved in any other previous case.
B. A. No. 1682 of 2016 2
4. I am not very much attracted by the above argument
of the learned counsel for the petitioner, since as correctly
pointed out the learned Public Prosecutor, huge quantity of koda
was recovered which rules out planting. It was from a place which
was close to her house. The petitioner was present at the time of
search and she could not be arrested because of the absence of
the Woman Police Constable.
Having regard to these facts I feel that this is not a fit case
for granting the benefit of pre-arrest bail. Bail application fails
and is dismissed.
Sd/-
SUNIL THOMAS, JUDGE.
/true copy/
P. A. to Judge
Pn

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits as

as well as the post mortem report.

3. The case of the prosecution, in short, is that the
petitioner has come to the house of the informant for giving her
his sister’s wedding card. At that time, he took her mobile
number and whatsapp number and started talking and chatting
with her and in the month of September 2023, he managed her
interview in a company for job. In October 2023, the informant
got the job at Samastipur. In meanwhile, the informant
established close relationship with him and also started trusting
