2/3
him. When she started working at Samastipur, due to the
relationship they liking each other. It is further alleged that the
petitioner has established physical relationship with her on the
false promise of marriage and that he has made her
objectionable video and has threatened her that he will ruin her.
4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the
petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has
committed no offence. He has been falsely implicated in this
case. From the F.I.R. itself it is clear that the relationship was
consensual one as according to the F.I.R., the relationship has
started in year 2023 and they had physical relationship many
time. The last physical relationship as reported by the informant
in 29th August 2025. On 07.09.2025, it is alleged that petitioner
has sent her video on her mobile and has threatened her. It has
further been submitted that all these go to show that there was
no objection on the part of the informant from the relationship
and intercourse thereafter but only allegation is that the obscene
video was sent on her mobile and was being threatened that the
petitioner will not marry her. It has also been submitted that this
is a case wherein two adults came into relationship and breakup
thereafter. It has further been submitted that this case has been
filed only with a view to pressurize the petitioner to solemnize

marriage with the informant. Petitioner is having no criminal
antecedent and he is languishing in judicial custody since

head:
02.02.2021
ss W.P.A. 14040 of 2019
(Through Video Conference)
,
Mrittika Purkait & ors.
Vs.
The State of West Bengal & ors.
Ms. Sumita Sarkar …. for the petitioners
Dr. S. K. Patra
Mr. K. K. Bandopadhyay
Ms. Supriya Dubey Chakraborty
… for the Commission
The learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that
the present writ petition has been preferred challenging the selection
process pertaining to the 1st State Level Selection Test, 2016 for
recruitment to the post of assistant teachers in Upper Primary Schools
in the State of West Bengal.
By a judgment delivered on 11th December, 2020 in similar
matters, a coordinate Bench of this Court has set aside and cancelled
the selection process for appointment of candidates to the post of
assistant teachers of Upper Primary Schools in the State of West
Bengal pursuant to the notification published for the said posts on 23rd
September, 2016.
In view thereof, no further order is required to be passed in the
present writ petition and the same is, accordingly, disposed of.
Since no affidavit-in-opposition is called for, allegations made
in the writ petition are deemed not to have been admitted.
All parties are to act on website copy of this order.
(Shekhar B. Saraf, J.)

CRL.P.NO.8136 OF 2016
O R D E R
This criminal petition is filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking to
quash the proceedings in Crime No.124/2016 on the file of Police Station,
Sangareddy ®, Medak Distraict, registered against the petitioner for the
offence punishable under Sections 354(a), 354(b), 406 and 509 of IPC.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional
Public Prosecutor appearing for the State.
A perusal of the complaint reveals that specific allegations were made
against the petitioner. This is a matter, which requires investigation by the
police. The truth or otherwise of the allegations can only be decided during
course of investigation or trial. I see no ground to interdict the investigation at
this stage and quash the first information report.
In the facts and circumstances of the case and as requested by the
learned counsel for the petitioner, the criminal petition is disposed of,
directing the investigating agency to proceed with the investigation.
However, for a period of two month from today, the petitioner shall not be
arrested.
Miscellaneous petitions pending if any, shall stand closed. No costs.
------------------------------
M.S.K.JAISWAL,J
DATE:16.06.2016
AVS

head:
Writ Petition no. 780 (S/S) of 2003
Vinod Kumar Devrani ------ Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttaranchal and others Respondents
Hon’ble M.M. Ghildiyal J.
The petitioner who is a Junior Engineer in the Rural Engineering
Services has been transferred from Doiwala district Dehradun to district
Uttarkashi. The contention of the petitioner is that his wife was operated for
brain tumor in P.G.D. Hospital Chandigarh in 1986 and since then she is not
in good condition and permanently under treatment of Himalya Joligrant
Dehradun. Apart from that the petitioner is also having his mother of 80
years and no body is to look after the wife and the mother as his son was
selected for four years course in engineering and is getting the said course at
Allahabad.
In view of the above circumstances it is a fit case where the authority
concerned should consider sympathetically. The petitioner has also moved
representation dated 26.7.2003 annexure 6 to the writ petition which is still
pending. The respondents are directed to decide the representation of the
petitioner sympathetically within a period of six weeks from the date of
production of certified copy of this order. Till the representation is decided
the petitioner shall not be relieved from the present post.
With these observations the writ petition is finally disposed of.
August 08,2003
MPS
(M.M. Ghildiyal, J.)

Hon'ble Umesh Kumar,J.
This writ petition has been filed, inter alia, for
the following relief:
" (I) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the respondents
not to demolish / acquire the house no. 175A
without adopting prescribed legal procedure as
per law."
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the
case, this writ petition is finally disposed of
granting liberty to the petitioner to approach the
appropriate authority i.e. the respondent no. 2,
District Magistrate, Gorakhpur by filing an
application for redressal of his grievances
within a week from today and in case any such
application is filed, the said authority would
look into the matter and pass appropriate order
after examining the matter in accordance with
law after giving opportunity of hearing to the
parties concerned within three weeks from the
date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
It is made clear that this court has not expressed
any opinion on the merits of the case and the
said authority has to take decision on its own
merits.
Order Date :- 26.8.2019

HON'BLE ASHUTOSH SRIVASTAVA, J.
Heard Shri Mukesh Joshi, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri R. K.
Nishad, learned Brief Holder for the State-respondents and perused the
record.
This bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita, 2023 has been moved on behalf of accused-applicant, Kasim,
seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 186 of 2022, under Sections
3, 5, 8 of U.P. Prevention of Cow Slaughter Act, Police Station Bhagatpur,
District Moradabad during the pendency of the trial before the Court below.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the accused-applicant is
innocent. He has been falsely implicated in this very case crime number and
is languishing in jail since 29.8.2025. Learned counsel for the applicant
submits that applicant was neither present nor arrested from the spot. His
name surfaced on record on the basis of confessional statement of co-
accused. He has 06 cases of criminal antecedent, which have sufficiently
been explained and there is no likelihood of his fleeing from course of
justice or tampering with evidence in case of release on bail. Hence, bail has
been prayed for.
Learned Brief Holder has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
Considering all above facts and circumstances, the nature of accusations,
severity of the punishment in the case of conviction and nature of supporting
evidence, reasonable apprehension of tampering with the witness and prima
facie case, but without commenting on merit of case, a case for bail is made
Versus

Counsel for Opposite Party(s) : G.A.

number be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and two
reliable sureties each, in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court
concerned, subject to the following conditions:
1. The applicant will not tamper with the evidence.

THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE M.SATHYANARAYANAN

Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of
India, seeking for a writ of mandamus, to direct the 1st, 2nd and 3rd
respondents to forthwith settle the retiral benefits and pension by
calculating the fixation of pay, increment, grade pay, with effect
form 01.01.2006 and to disburse the same with interest at 24% per
annum from the date on which the same fell due till the date of
realization on the basis of the representation dated 25.04.2015 and
03.06.2015.
For Petitioner : Mr.L.Chandrakumar
For RR 1 to 3 : Mr.R.Vijayakumar, AGP
O R D E R
By consent, the writ petition is taken up for final disposal.
2.The petitioner would state that she was appointed as Sanitary
Worker on 24.02.1988 and after declaration of probation on
23.02.1989, she was absorbed in the said post with effect from her
date of initial appointment, i.e., from 24.02.1988. The petitioner
has attained the age of superannuation and was permitted to retire
vide proceedings of the 3rd respondent dated 30.04.2015. The
grievance expressed by the petitioner is that so far, the pensionary
benefits have not been disbursed and though disciplinary proceedingshttps://hcservices.ecourts.gov.in/hcservices/
have been initiated against her on account of her alleged absence, it
was culminated with “warning” and therefore, there is no impediment
on the part of the respondents to disburse the pensionary benefits
due and payable to the petitioner and in this regard, she has
submitted representations on 25.04.2015 and on 03.06.2015 and since
no response is forthcoming, she came forward to file this writ
petition.
3.Mr.L.Chandrakumar, learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that since the petitioner was administered with “warning”, it
does not amount to punishment and hence, there may not be any
impediment on the part of the respondents 1 to 3 to favourably
consider the representations submitted by the petitioner for
disbursement of pensionary benefits and since the said exercise has
not been done so far, the petitioner is also entitled to get interest
at the rate of 24% per annum from the date on which the pensionary
benefits are due and payable to her and prays for appropriate orders.
4.Heard the submissions of Mr.R.Vijayakumar, learned Additional
Government Pleader who accepts notice on behalf of the respondents.
5.This Court, taking into consideration the above facts and
circumstances and without going into the merits of the claim
projected by the petitioner, directs the 1st respondent to consider
and dispose of the petitioner's representations dated 25.04.2015 and
03.06.2015 on merits and in accordance with law and pass orders
within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of
this order and communicate the decision taken, to the petitioner
herein.
6.The writ petition is disposed of accordingly. No costs.

Court No. - 75
Case :- WRIT - C No. - 32993 of 2021
Petitioner :- Smt. Lalita
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Santosh Kumar Pandey,Sudhir
Shukla
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Dinesh Pathak,J.
Heard learned counsel for the parties through virtual mode.
Present writ petition has been filed beseeching expeditious
disposal of Mutation Case No. 752 of 2015 (Lalita Devi vs.
Onkar Nath), under Section 34 of U.P. Revenue Code 2006,
pending in the Court of Tehsildar (respondent no. 2).
It is submitted that mutation application filed by the petitioner
under Section 34 of U.P. Revenue Code, 2006 is pending since
May, 2015 despite the fact that statutory period for deciding the
same, as enunciated under Rule 34(7) of U.P. Revenue Code
Rules, 2016, has already been elapsed. It is further submitted
that both the parties have already appeared in the aforesaid
matter and the case is ready for final adjudication.
Learned Standing Counsel has no objection in case the
aforesaid case is directed to be decided within a stipulated
period fixed by this Court.
In this conspectus as above, no useful purpose would be served
to keep this matter pending, therefore, this court deems it
appropriate to finally dispose of the present writ petition,
without making any observation on the merits of the case as
mentioned in the present writ petition, with a direction to the
Tehsildar (Respondent No. 2), before whom the case is pending,
to decide the same expeditiously, preferably, within a period of
three months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this
order.
It is expected that it should be decided by reasoned and
speaking order, in accordance with law, after affording
opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned without granting
unnecessary adjournments.
With the aforesaid direction, present writ petition is disposed of.
Order Date :- 12.1.2022

head:
A.F.R.
Court No. - 11
Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 12363
of 2021
Applicant :- Nirmala Second Bail
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Naresh Chandra,Paltoo Ram Gupta
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
1. Heard Sri P.R. Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant and
Ms. Kiran Singh, learned A.G.A.
2. This is the second bail application. First bail application was
rejected on 18.3.2021 by Hon'ble Vikas Kunvar Srivastav, J.
vide Bail No.3356 of 2021.
3. In view of the order of Hon'ble the Chief Justice dated
13.11.2018, if the Hon'ble Court, which has rejected the bail
application of an accused, is not sitting at the place where
subsequent bail application has been filed, the same shall be put
up before the regular Court, therefore, this bail application has
been put up before the regular Court. It has been noted that the
Hon'ble Court, which has rejected the first bail application, is
presently not sitting at Lucknow where this second bail
application has been filed.
4. As per Sri Gupta, the present applicant, who is a lady, is in
jail since 24.11.2020 in Case Crime No.0206 of 2020, under
Sections 147, 323, 302/34, 336 & 506 IPC, Police Station –
Asoha, District – Unnao.
5. Sri Gupta has submitted that he is conscious about the fact
that he cannot raise any arguments or take any ground in the
second bail application, which could have been taken in the first
bail application, therefore, he shall not be repeating any
arguments or grounds, which have already been considered by
this Court while rejecting the first bail application of the present
applicant on 18.3.2021.
6. Sri Gupta has submitted that he shall be pressing this second
bail application on the solitary ground that after rejection of bail
application of the present applicant on 18.3.2021, this Court
granted bail to co-accused Bahadur in Bail No.7523 of 2021 on
5.10.2021. Further, other co-accused persons, namely, Bablu
has been granted bail in Bail No.5287 of 2021 on 9.11.2021;
Kamal has been granted bail in Bail No.12888 of 2021 on
22.11.2021 and Deepu has been granted bail in Bail No.8149 of
2021 on 7.12.2021 as orders of those accused persons have
been shown to the Court, which are taken on record.
7. Sri Gupta has drawn attention of this Court towards the
decision of Division Bench of this Court in re; Nanha S/O
Nabhan Kha vs. State of U.P., reported in 1993 CriLJ 938,
wherein the question was considered as to whether any accused
may be entitled for bail in his/her subsequent bail application, if
after rejection of his/her bail, the other co-accused persons have
been granted bail. In para-1 of the judgment, the aforesaid
question has been indicated, which reads as under:-
1. In the third bail application moved by the petitioner for bail in case
Crime No. 53 of 1989 under Section 302, IPC of P.S. Ganj, district
Rampur Hon'ble N.L. Ganguli, J. has referred the following question to a
larger Bench for an authoritative pronouncement:--
"Whether an accused is entitled to be released on bail on the ground of
parity by moving a second or third bail application in a circumstance that
at a later date a co-accused of the same criminal case with a similar role
was granted bail by the another Hon'ble Judge before whom without
disclosing the fact that the bail application of another co- accused with
similar role had already been rejected, by another Bench, bail was
granted."
8. While replying the aforesaid question, the Devision Bench of
this Court in re; Nanha (supra) has observed in paragraphs 53
& 58 as under:-

The petitioner is the manager of a Private Educational
institution which has an electricity connection. Their grievance
of the petitioner in this writ petition is that they are being
charged to electricity under LT VIIA Tariff, whereas this court
has, in the decision of Bro. Joseph Antony v. Kerala State
Electricity Board [2009(3) KLT 1022] held that private
educational institutions are liable to pay electricity charges only
under LT VI A Tariff. The petitioner therefore seeks the

quash that part of the Tariff Order classifying self-
financing educational institutions under LT VII A Tariff;

(a) and other bills, issued on the basis of Board Order
(FM) No. 2731/2007/KSEB/TRAC/Tariff Rev. 07-08 dated
01.12.2007.

KSERC as per Ext.P1 to the extent it classifies
educational institutions into Government. Aided private
educational institutions (under LT VI A) and self-
financing educational institutions (under LT VIIA
commercial) for the purpose of charging electricity is
illegal and violative of Sec.62(3) of the Electricity Act,
2003;
W.P(C) No. 34914 of 2009 -2-

institution is not liable to be billed under LT VII A
commercial tariff and that the tariff applicable to
petitioner's institution is LT VI A;

to adjust it in the future bills of the petitioner.”

Electricity Board would contend that in an SLP filed before the

District Collector, Malappuram and another [2009 (4) KHC
283 (DB)] held that, even when a decision of the Division Bench

Judges of this court are bound by the law laid down by the

excess mount paid by the petitio

Heard the parties.
Apprehending his arrest in connection with Sadar P.S. Case No.500 of
2018 corresponding to G.R. No.117 of 2019 instituted under Sections 147, 148,
341, 323, 337, 338, 307, 332, 333, 435, 427, 353, 295A, 135A, 109, 120B, 188, 149
of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Prevention of Damage to
Public Property Act, 1984, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of
privileges of anticipatory bail.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the
allegation against the petitioner is that there was an incident of stone pelting
between the two communities and one of the community was inter alia
headed by the petitioner and the co-accused persons and the people of his
community were raising anti-religious slogans to hurt the sentiments of a
class of the citizens of India and by such pelting of stones, many peoples
were injured and further the petitioner and the co-accused persons blocked
the road and used criminal force against the public officials deterring them
from discharging their duties. It is further submitted that the allegations
against the petitioner are general and omnibus in nature and are false. It is
then submitted that the petitioner was not present at the place of occurrence
and he has been implicated in this case only because he is a permanent
resident of the locality. It is also submitted that the co-accused, with similar
allegations, has already been given the privileges of anticipatory bail by this
Court vide order dated 08.07.2019 passed in A.B.A. No.3925 of 2019. It is
lastly submitted that the petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the
investigation of the case and to furnish sufficient security including cash
security. Hence, it is submitted that on the principle of parity, the petitioner
be also given the privileges of anticipatory bail
Learned P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for
anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
Considering the submissions of learned counsels and the facts and
circumstances stated above, I am inclined to grant privileges of anticipatory
bail to the petitioner. Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in
the Court below within six weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or
surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on depositing Rs.5,000/- as cash
security and on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty five thousand)
with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned C.J.M.,
Hazaribag in connection with Sadar P.S. Case No.500 of 2018 corresponding
to G.R. No.117 of 2019 with the condition that he will co-operate with the
investigation of the case and appear before the investigating officer as and
when noticed by him and furnish his mobile number and photocopy of
the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile
number during the pendency of the case and further conditions as laid
down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

This application has been filed under Article 227 of the
Constitution of India for a direction to the Court below to dispose
of petition dated 24.06.2015 filed in Title Suit No.201 of 2014.
The Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Radhey
Shyam and Ors. vs. Chhabi Nath and Ors., (2015) 5 Supreme
Court Cases 423 has held that control of working of the
subordinate courts in dealing with their judicial order is exercised
by way of appellate or revisional power or power of
superintendence under Article 227. While appellate or revisional
jurisdiction is regulated by the statute, the power of
superintendence under Article 227 is constitutional.
In view of this decision of the Supreme Court, the
working of the subordinate courts in dealing with their judicial
Patna High Court C.Misc. No.1604 of 2016 (2) dt.16-01-2017
2
order can only be examined under Article 227 of the Constitution
of India in judicial side.
It is well settled principles of law that High Court also
exercises supervisory jurisdiction in administrative side under
Article 227 of the Constitution of India as has been held by the
Supreme Court in (2010) 8 Supreme Court Cases 329.
In the present case, no order has been produced so that
in judicial side the High Court cannot pass any such order blankly.
If so advised, the petitioner may approach the court concerned for
expeditious disposal of the case.
Accordingly, this civil miscellaneous application is
dismissed.

promotion avenue was available to the Multipurpose
Health Worker (Male) on the day the petitioner
became entitled to have the first selection grade, as
such selection grade is required to be given to the
petitioner as per para-5 of the Government of
Rajasthan circular dated 17.2.1998. Under the
notification aforesaid, the pay-scale applicable for the
petitioner is Rs.4000-6000. The respondents,
therefore, erroneously m
tail:
d to be given to the
petitioner as per para-5 of the Government of
Rajasthan circular dated 17.2.1998. Under the
notification aforesaid, the pay-scale applicable for the
petitioner is Rs.4000-6000. The respondents,
therefore, erroneously made fixation of the
petitioner's pay in the pay-scale of Rs.3200-4900
after awarding first selection grade.
As a matter of fact, the issue involved in this
petition for writ has already been adjudicated earlier
in the case of Asha Ram & Anr. Vs. State of Rajasthan
& Ors., (S.B. Civil Writ Petition No.5333/2006 decided
on 17.5.2013).
Having considered all the facts of the case, this
petition for writ for the reasons given deserves to be
accepted. Accordingly, the same is allowed. The
respondents are directed to allow first selection grade
to the petitioner in the pay-scale of Rs.4000-6000
w.e.f. 11.2.1991 and second & third selection grades
in terms of para-5 of the circulars dated 25.1.1992
and 17.2.1998. No order as to costs.”
(4 of 4) [CW-3069/2021]

shall be satisfied if their representation is decided by the
respondents in light of the aforequoted precedent of DadamDas
Vaishnav (supra).
In light of the aforequoted judgment, the writ petition is
disposed of with the direction to the respondents to decide the
representation of the petitioners in terms of aforementioned
judgment within a period of 30 days from today strictly in
accordance with law.

head:
Court No. - 39
Case :- WRIT - C No. - 35705 of 2022
Petitioner :- Famuddin And 2 Others
Respondent :- Union Of India And 10 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- S.M. Iqbal Hasan,Mohammad Zakir
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Kiran Bala
Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Chandra Kumar Rai,J.
Sri Kiran Bala learned counsel appears for the respondent no.1
and learned Standing counsel for the State respondent.
The challenge is to the order dated 11.5.2022 passed by the
respondent no.2 namely the competent authority/ Additional
District Magistrate (Finance and Revenue) Muzzaffarnagar in
the matter of disbursement of compensation under Section
3H(3) of the National Highways Act.
Sri S.M. Iqbal Hasan, learned counsel for the petitioners, at the
outset, submits that the competent authority has no jurisdiction
to decide the dispute related to apportionment of compensation
amongst the co-sharer and in case of dispute raised by any of
the co sharer, it was required to refer the matter before the
competent court in accordance with the provisions of Section
3H-4 of the National Highways Act.
It is then argued that there is no dispute with regard to the
family settlement dated 13.1.1960 which was the claim of the
petitioners herein to grant compensation to the exclusion of
other co-sharers. It is argued that this Court and the Apex Court
from time and again have held that the family settlement cannot
be disputed in the court of law. Reliance has been placed on the
decision of the Apex Court in Ravinder Kaur Grewal vs
Manjit Kaur and others reported in AIR Online 2020 SC
669.
Noticing the above submissions of the learned counsel for the
petitioner, suffice it to note that the petitioners herein are
claiming their exclusive right over the land in question on the
basis of the family settlement dated 13.1.1960 which has not
seen the light of the day till the objection has been filed by the
petitioner in the matter of apportionment of compensation to the
other co-sharers. The order impugned categorically records that
all the co-sharers are owners-in-possession of the property in
question which is Khasra no.1248 and it was the joint property
of the co-sharers as their names are indicated in the revenue
records. The petitioners herein had filed a case under Section
116 of the Revenue Code, 2006 which was not pressed by them
and was dismissed as such. The objections were taken by other
co-sharers about the family settlement dated 13.1.1960 that it is
a result of fraud and fabrication made by the petitioners herein.
Be that as it may, the order impugned records that there is no
partition of the property in question by the competent court and
moreover, the family settlement has not been acknowledged in
any Court of law to grant exclusive rights to the petitioners. The
filing of the civil suit before the Civil Court would not be a
reason to deny compensation to the recorded co-tenure holders
of the plot in question.
Noticing the above, we do not find it a fit case for interference.
Reliance placed on the decision of the Apex Court is of no
benefit to the petitioners in view of the fact that there is a
dispute with regard to the genuineness of the family settlement
dated 13.1.1960.
The pendency of the civil suit, admittedly, is of no relevance. In
so far as the disbursement of compensation is concerned no
valid dispute could be raised by the petitioners before the
competent authority and as such it was not under obligation to
refer the matter to the civil court.
The writ petition is, accordingly, dismissed being devoid of
merits.

CRIMINAL MISC. WRIT PETITION No. - 20683 of 2025
Court No. - 43
HON'BLE SIDDHARTHA VARMA, J.
HON'BLE ABDUL SHAHID, J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned AGA for the State.
2. Although, the prayer made in this writ petition is to quash the First
Information Report dated 19.3.2025 giving rise to Case Crime No.142 of
2025, under Sections 115(2), 352, 351(2) and 324(4) of Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita, 2023, Police Station - Handia, District - Prayagraj but at the time
when the matter is taken up learned counsel for the petitioners confines his
relief to grant of protection under section 35 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita.
3. We have perused the the First Information Report, which prima facie
discloses commissioning of cognizable offence and, therefore, the prayer
made to quash F.I.R. otherwise cannot be entertained in view of the law laid
down by the Supreme Court in the case of State of Telangana Vs. Habib
Abdullah Jellani, (2017) 2 SCC 779 and Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra and Others, (2021) SCC Online SC 315.
4. We are of the view that no interference is warranted.
5. However, considering the fact that all offences mentioned in the present
case are punishable with a term up to 7 years, the authorities are directed to
ensure the procedure of arrest as per the guidelines of the Supreme Court
enshrined in the case of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar reported in
(2014) 8 SCC 273.

for bonus marks to eligible candidates on the basis of experience
gained on prescribed conditions and for the purpose of claiming
bonus marks candidates are required to upload experience
certificate in prescribed proforma duly issued by the competent
authority (CMHO concerned).
4. Their main grievance is, that in spite of the fact that they
have applied for issuance of experience certificate which is
mandatory for claiming bonus marks for the post of Nursing
Officer, the concerned CMHO/authorities are not issuing them
experience certificates due to which they are not able to submit
their online application forms.
5. While pointing out that thousands of applicants have applied
for experience certificate and there are limited resources and
manpower to deal with such huge number of applications in short
span of time, learned counsel submitted that in absence of clear

guidelines and yardsticks, the CMHOs are taking longer than usual
time and precaution while issuing experience certificates. It was
also contended that in many cases they are verbally refusing to
issue certificates citing that the applicant is not entitled for bonus
marks.
6. It is brought to the notice of the Court by the learned
counsel for the petitioners that in view of the stipulation carved in
the circular dated 05.12.2022 particularly "ik= vH;fFkZ;ksa", the
CMHO concerned are raising all types of queries/hurdles and
making it almost impossible to obtain an experience certificate.
7. It was argued that though the entitlement for bonus marks is
to be determined by the competent authority/recruitment
authority at the time of document verification or preparation of
merit list, but the CMHOs have taken unto themselves the task of
adjudging the eligibility of each candidate.
8. Considering the grievance of the petitioners, this Court had
directed the Joint Director (Recruitment) Medical & Health to
remain present so that the concern expressed and issues raised
by the petitioners can be appropriately addressed.

For the Petitioners : Mr.Vinay Ranjan, Advocate

======================================================
CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE MADHURESH PRASAD
ORAL ORDER
2 08-07-2020 Since as of now the Courts have not resumed normal
physical hearing, the matter has been listed today for
consideration through video conferencing.
The learned counsels are appearing and making
submissions from their residence. The Court Master and
Secretary are also part of this virtual Court proceedings from
their homes, all with the aid of audio visual technology.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and the
learned APP for the State.
The petitioners are apprehending their arrest in
connection with Warisnagar P.S. Case No.234 of 2019 registered
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.7598 of 2020(2) dt.08-07-2020
2/3
for the offence punishable under Sections 363 and 366 of the
Indian Penal Code, which is pending in the court of the learned
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Samastipur.
The informant has alleged that his daughter was
married with Shivam Kumar, son of Petitioner Nos.1 and 3, on
31.10.2018. There is allegation that Petitioner Nos.1 and 3 along
with their son have been demanding a motorcycle and
subjecting the informant’s daughter to torture, not allowing her
to meet her parents and that on 29.08.2019 when the informant
along with his brother went to meet his daughter, they were not
allowed to meet, by the petitioners. It is further alleged that on
30.08.2019, the informant came to know that the petitioners had
killed his daughter and concealed her dead body.
Petitioners’ counsel submits that it is a false case. In
fact, the victim and son of Petitioner Nos.1 and 3 had
solemnized a love marriage. The story regarding demand of
motorcycle is palpably false. Brother-in-law of the informant
Shyam Nandan Singh, with whom the petitioners are on
litigating terms, has conspired to implicate the petitioners.
Learned APP for the State has opposed the prayer for
pre-arrest bail. It is submitted that there is specific allegation
that these petitioners had taken the victim away to an isolated
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.7598 of 2020(2) dt.08-07-2020
3/3
place where she was forcibly kept in confinement for more than
one month. To this extent, the victim herself has given her
statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
Considering the rival submissions and the gravity of
the allegations, this Court does not find it to be a fit case for
grant of anticipatory bail. It is, accordingly, rejected.
PNM
(Madhuresh Prasad, J)
U T
